classification.difficultyReason: Read the sign of displacement and interpret the sign or zero value of the gradient as velocity in five qualitative graphs.

content.prompt: Describe the displacement and velocity of the particle at $t_1$ for each displacement graph.

spec.description: Upward-opening displacement curve with its second time-axis crossing at t₁; a minimum lies below the axis before t₁. No numerical scale or grid is supplied.
spec.mathematics: At t₁ the displacement is zero and the gradient is positive.

answer.short: $x(t_1)=0$ and $v(t_1)>0$: at the origin, moving in the positive direction.
answer.worked: At $t_1$ the curve crosses the time axis, so $x(t_1)=0$. Its gradient is positive, so $v(t_1)>0$. The particle is at the origin and moving in the positive direction.

spec.description: Downward-opening displacement curve, initially below the time axis, with a positive maximum directly above t₁ and a downward continuation arrow.
spec.mathematics: At t₁ displacement is positive and the horizontal tangent gives zero velocity.

answer.short: $x(t_1)>0$ and $v(t_1)=0$: on the positive side of the origin and at rest.
answer.worked: At $t_1$ the curve is above the time axis, so $x(t_1)>0$. The tangent at the maximum is horizontal, so $v(t_1)=0$. The particle is on the positive side of the origin and momentarily at rest.

spec.description: Curve rises from negative displacement to a positive maximum, falls to a negative minimum, then rises. The t₁ marker is below the descending negative-displacement section before the minimum.
spec.mathematics: At t₁ displacement and velocity are both negative.

answer.short: $x(t_1)<0$ and $v(t_1)<0$: on the negative side of the origin, moving in the negative direction.
answer.worked: At $t_1$ the curve is below the time axis, so $x(t_1)<0$. The curve is falling, so its gradient and $v(t_1)$ are negative. The particle is moving farther from the origin in the negative direction.

spec.description: Displacement curve with two positive maxima separated by a negative minimum; the second maximum is higher. The t₁ marker is after the second maximum and before the last crossing, where displacement remains positive and the curve falls.
spec.mathematics: At t₁ displacement is positive and velocity is negative.

answer.short: $x(t_1)>0$ and $v(t_1)<0$: on the positive side of the origin, moving towards it.
answer.worked: At $t_1$ the curve is above the time axis, so $x(t_1)>0$. Its gradient is negative, so $v(t_1)<0$. The particle is on the positive side of the origin and moving towards the origin.

spec.description: Curve starts at positive displacement, rises to a positive maximum, falls through the time axis to a negative minimum directly below t₁, then rises through the axis.
spec.mathematics: At t₁ displacement is negative and the horizontal tangent gives zero velocity.

answer.short: $x(t_1)<0$ and $v(t_1)=0$: on the negative side of the origin and at rest.
answer.worked: At $t_1$ the curve is below the time axis, so $x(t_1)<0$. The tangent at the minimum is horizontal, so $v(t_1)=0$. The particle is on the negative side of the origin and momentarily at rest.
